title: Senior AI Research Engineer at Agility Robotics Believes NVIDIA Ecosystem Leads in Embodied AI Hardware Solutions
expert: Senior AI Research Engineer at Agility Robotics (current); one of three hardware decision-makers for a ~20-person embodied-AI team; interview 2026-08-12
verdict: An Agility Robotics senior AI engineer, one of three hardware decision-makers, says a rival needs >20% better inference latency and ~10% more VRAM just to be considered, and the team is moving to NVIDIA Jetson (likely Thor).

Compute share vs. XPU/ASIC: 🟢 **Switching bar: >20% latency gain plus ~10% more VRAM**; porting is the "very biggest hidden cost"; first read on edge switching thresholds. → Tenet 3 (~75% share) ↑
🟢 **Agility moving from older NVIDIA GPUs to Jetson, likely Thor**; no other vendor seriously considered. → Tenet 4 (new TAM vectors) ↑
Demand / orders (edge AI): 🟢 **World models now 10-20 billion parameters** vs VLAs under 1B to a couple of billion, too big for one edge device, pushing work to cloud and lab GPUs (5090/4090).
🟢 **Inference is 90% of end-to-end robot latency** (sensors ~7%, actuation 3%), so compute is the binding constraint.

changes: First read on edge-AI switching thresholds and robot latency split; no earlier expert call or stored row.
thesis_impact: Tenet 3 (~75% share): ↑ — at the edge, a rival needs >20% latency and ~10% VRAM gains plus equal tooling to be considered.
Tenet 4 (new TAM vectors): ↑ — Agility moving to Jetson Thor; world models scaling to 10-20B parameters.
